scope: All six Table 1 mortars (Ctrl and 0.2–1.0 vol% PP fibre) with the shared g/kg batch, the Table 3 split-Hopkinson peak stress of each mortar at four impact pressures, and the control flow. Static strengths are plotted only in Figure 4.

materials.name: River sand
materials.detail: River sand was used as the fine aggregate in this study, with a fineness modulus of 2.36 and an apparent density of 3000 kg/m3.

materials.name: PPFs
materials.detail: PPFs with lengths of 13 mm, diameter of 150 µm and density of 0.91 g/cm3 were used in this research [26].

cures.text: Subsequently, the mortar, sealed in the molds, is placed in a curing room with a humidity level of no less than 95% and a temperature of (20 ± 2) °C for 24 h. For specimens with uneven surfaces, it is necessary to use a grinding machine for surface treatment before placing the specimens back in the curing room for continued curing.

gaps: Table 1 is in g/kg of mortar (recorded as mass parts); the activator is one solution (modulus 1.8, 20% solids) made from Na2SiO3, NaOH and water. Fibre is dosed by volume of the total mixture.

Table 3 names specimens "PPF-0.0%-1 … PPF-1.0%-4"; the 0.0% series is the Ctrl mix and the suffix is the impact-pressure index (0.35, 0.45, 0.55, 0.65 MPa), quoted as each result's condition. Strain rate, toughness, peak strain and DIF are not transcribed.
Static compressive strength at 3, 7 and 28 days is only in Figure 4; flow values other than Ctrl are stated by fibre content without the group label (0.2%: 248 mm; 1.0%: 224 mm).
